approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules. It draws parents from high-scoring population bands, combines connected fragments or applies ordinary local mutations and short mutation walks, and keeps a bounded population of the best scored survivors. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities and duplicate rejection precede a sulfur introduction gate: an outside-envelope local signature cannot exceed its largest multiplicity in the actual original scored generating parents. Bounded refill produces a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to the full chronological accepted archive uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity. Each batch position chooses the remaining maximizer of a correlated score draw; accepted feedback updates both the prediction archive and breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove only cross-candidate residual dependence during allocation. Each original standard normal receives its candidate’s existing jittered marginal standard deviation, obtained from the complete Cholesky row, while the full fitted joint model and nonzero random excursions remain. This revisits the earlier correlation control on the sulfur-gated Parent, whose changed admission and ancestry require a current conditional contribution answer. Completed siblings changed mean geometry, residual geometry, squared covariance or the composite selector; none removes original dependence while preserving original jittered marginals. The new test identifies that single boundary, with no chemical diversity objective or changed predictor.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent's limiting behavior for this question is that correlated allocation excursions still couple candidate identities, while their useful conditional endpoint contribution remains unidentified after the sulfur gate changed admissible pools and ancestry. Its three actual per-seed summary.json/run.log pairs are complete and successful, with macro mean 0.59645311428869, population deviation 0.03397032998399878 and seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917. The published gate analysis records 435 full pools, 130 rejected positive-excess opportunities and unchanged correlated allocation; its gate increment +0.0007834645552323346 is below the supplied 0.002 scale and includes a losing seed. Code inspection shows full fitted conditional covariance and jittered Cholesky residuals entering masked maxima. This establishes presence, not current isolated correlation value. Historical n-54adc6a641e8 preserved jittered marginals and changed 422/435 same-input batch sets, but removal lost 0.018447481386582327 against ungated n-62daf219c70a, with seed changes -0.06643859903696303, +0.03550275965606198 and -0.02440660477884593 and five improving task-seed cells. The current gated composite removal n-605c7a785b51 lost 0.12818290031998167, with fourteen losing cells, but cannot identify residual constituents. Current exponential-residual substitution n-6ebafca203bf changed 318 sets and lost 0.02971005981260903 while retaining original means; its changed marginal law likewise does not isolate original dependence. These are limits on attribution and local productivity proxies, not evidence of harmful covariance or broken factorization.
hypothesis: Remove only original cross-candidate dependence from allocation residual draws by multiplying each original standard normal by the corresponding full Cholesky row norm, preserving the Parent’s actual jittered marginal variances, nonzero residual influence and fitted full count-based joint posterior.

finding_summary.headline: Correlation removal executed exactly and lowered mean score by 0.0505, all three seeds worse: correlated draws help the sulfur-gated Parent
finding_summary.insights:
This answers the open component question for the current Parent. On the sulfur-gated composition, letting similar candidates share their sampled noise is worth about 0.05 of mean final score. Under the registered rule, that is a positive conditional contribution of cross-candidate residual correlation. The same removal on the earlier, ungated Parent cost 0.018 and had one gaining seed; here every seed loses. These two results come from different Parents and are not an interaction estimate. The result is descriptive, from three seeds, and not uniform: sitagliptin_mpo and median_2 gained in two seeds each.

The replays on identical pools show what correlation does at a single decision. Without it, the chosen batch of ten looks more alike to the model: average absolute model correlation within the batch rises from 0.051 to 0.055, and the reverse replay on Parent pools shows the same shift. The batch also sits slightly farther from already-scored molecules, while molecule size and the crossover share barely change. Correlated noise therefore spreads each batch across regions the model treats as distinct. These per-decision differences are small, but they compound. Histories diverge from the first batch, and on two tasks they drift toward large, sprawling molecules. On those two tasks, the Molecular review finds that the Child's higher-scoring molecules are the smaller ones. This is the third allocation change in this lineage to show the same pattern: more local wins but less total progress (the earlier ungated removal and the exponential-residual substitution showed it too). Parent-beat counts and new-scaffold counts should not be read as evidence of useful exploration here.

Open questions remain. The size drift accompanies the biggest losses, but it is an association, not a demonstrated cause. In five of fifteen Child runs the sulfur gate never fired, and their scored trajectories are byte-identical to the earlier ungated removal. Two whole task-seed comparisons repeat the earlier experiment exactly, although the remaining 13 still average -0.040. So this is not an independent replication, and it says nothing about whether the gate and correlation interact. Whether a stronger batch-diversity rule would beat correlated draws is untested. The result argues for keeping correlated allocation and, if anything, strengthening batch-level diversity. It also makes molecule-size control a candidate lever: unchecked growth accompanies the largest losses on two tasks and pushes scoring time toward the per-task limit.
finding_summary.results:
The change did exactly what it was meant to do and nothing else. In every one of the 435 batch decisions (five tasks, three seeds, 29 batches each) the fitted model still treated the candidates as related: 99.9% of candidate pairs had nonzero model covariance. Even so, the random draws that pick each batch were, exactly as specified, independent across candidates, each with that candidate's full posterior variance, and the model's means, uncertainties and factorization matched the Parent's code on identical inputs. The random numbers themselves were identical to the Parent's in every batch. The change mattered at almost every decision. Replaying the original correlated draws on the Child's own pools would have picked a different set of ten molecules in 422 of 435 batches, with an average overlap of 6.8 of 10. On the 15 first batches, where Child and Parent saw identical inputs, the replay reproduced the Parent's actual choices exactly. Sampled noise still steered 3,713 of 4,350 picks away from the highest predicted mean. Molecule generation, the sulfur gate, identity checks, the survivor population and the feedback loop were re-audited with no failures.

The final score fell from 0.5965 to 0.5459, a paired loss of 0.0505, far past the 0.002 decision scale. All three seeds lost (-0.087, -0.030, -0.035), and 10 of 15 task-seed endpoints fell. The largest drops were on drd2_docking seed 1 (-0.269) and deco_hop seed 0 (-0.253). Five rose: sitagliptin_mpo seed 1 by +0.153, and four by less than 0.01 (median_2 seeds 0 and 1, sitagliptin_mpo seed 2, deco_hop seed 1). By task, drd2_docking (-0.131), deco_hop (-0.100) and zaleplon_mpo (-0.037) fell, while median_2 (+0.002) and sitagliptin_mpo (+0.014) edged up. The three Child seed scores sit close together (standard deviation 0.010 against the Parent's 0.034): the Child is consistently lower, not just noisier.

Search behaviour changed in a mixed way. The Child logged more local wins: 680 offspring beat their best parent (Parent 648), 289 raised the running best (255), and 319 of the parent-beating offspring carried new scaffolds (262). But the material it worked from was weaker. Offspring averaged 0.299 against 0.372, their parents 0.367 against 0.455, and the total of all running-best improvements fell from 5.82 to 5.06. On deco_hop and drd2_docking, four of six Child runs drifted to much larger molecules: 47 to 83 heavy atoms on average, against 27 to 35 for the Parent. In those four runs 819 crossover attempts produced no molecule, each pairing two parents that together exceeded the 120-atom limit (the whole Parent panel had 2 such failures), and in one deco_hop run scoring took 92 minutes, inside the time limit. Ranking quality on the selected molecules was essentially unchanged: pair-ordering accuracy 0.70 against 0.71, rank correlation 0.81 against 0.81.

molecular.headline: Ring-dense halogenated aromatics whose top scorers run on N-halogen, O-halogen and cyanate-ester decoration
molecular.overall_character: Across all 4350 optimizer proposals read over five objectives and three Search Seeds every molecule parsed, and the sets are overwhelmingly cyclic and aromatic: digest ring_closure_rate 0.9644 to 0.9851 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9598 to 0.9770, with 2.9 to 8.2 rings and 2.1 to 7.0 aromatic rings per molecule. The element vocabulary is narrow - C, N, O, F, Cl, S, Br only, no phosphorus, boron or iodine - and heavily halogenated, digest halogen_rate 0.9816, 0.9448 and 0.8724 on three objectives. Two whole classes of chemistry are absent rather than rare: digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 everywhere while the molecules themselves average up to 2.19 undefined tetrahedral centres, and digest charged_rate is 0.0 everywhere, so no ionisable acid, no zwitterion and no quaternary nitrogen is ever proposed. The ten supplied starting molecules are ordinary medicinal chemistry - a prolinamide dichlorobenzenesulfonamide bearing a free acid, 'COc1cc(F)cc(-c2ccc(C(CC(=O)O)NC(=O)C3CCCN3S(=O)(=O)c3cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c3)cc2)c1', and a dimethoxy indole-2-carboxanilide, 'COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC' - and the search moves away from that vocabulary rather than elaborating it: carboxylic acids fall from 2 of the 10 seeds to 0.0 to 12.8 percent of proposals, saturated piperidine, piperazine and morpholine rings to 0.0 to 2.9 percent, and an unfused saturated six-carbon ring and a trifluoromethyl group each match exactly none of the 4350. What replaces them is bond-level halogen and heteroatom decoration. Against the Parent's trajectories read under the same procedure, this node's proposals are markedly larger and greasier on two objectives - proposals above 600 Da rise from 13.4 to 62.4 percent and from 10.0 to 50.8 percent, and the fraction meeting all four Lipinski criteria falls from 0.559 to 0.103 and from 0.321 to 0.072 - and carry fewer basic ring nitrogens on the two objectives whose own score gradient most rewards them, 66.4 to 37.4 percent and 69.5 to 44.9 percent. Both runs share the same structural blind spots, so these are drifts within one generator's repertoire, not a new repertoire. This is a description of the molecules only; scoring and activation are not mine to judge.

per_task.generated_character: Mid-sized, flat, fused bicyclic aromatics: mean 24.0 heavy atoms, 361 Da, 2.87 rings of which 2.54 are aromatic, fraction sp3 carbon 0.21, and 94.5 percent halogenated (digest halogen_rate 0.9448). The dominant frameworks are a 4,6-dimethoxyindole-2-carboxamide/amidine, the direct descendant of the seed molecule 'COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC' (0.3051), and a benzocyclobutene-acetamide. Within a seed the search is strongly converged: 83 to 114 distinct Murcko scaffolds over 290 proposals, but only 3 to 7 scaffolds among the thirty best, and the top band differs only in which halogen sits on which nitrogen - five molecules tie at 0.4276 as the Cl/F/Br permutations of one amidine.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds dominate the winners: 'COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=NBr)N(Br)c3ccccc3)cc2c(OC)c1C' at 0.4145 carries both an N-bromoamine and an N-bromoimine, neither an isolable compound
N-fluoro and N-bromo azole nitrogens, 'COc1cc2c(cc(C(=N)N(Cl)c3ccccc3)n2F)c(OC)c1C', put the halogen on the indole nitrogen itself
the single best molecule is a strained benzo-fused four-membered ring bearing an N-hydroxyanilide, 'Cc1cc2c(c(C)c1C)C=C2CC(=O)N(O)c1ccc(Br)nc1'
an S-N sulfenamide and a thiomethyl arene, 'COc1cc2c(c(SC)c1C)C=C2CC(=O)N(S)c1ccc(Cl)nc1'
3.3 percent of proposals are degenerate one- to three-atom fragments that score zero and still consume an oracle call: 'C1COO1', 'OO', 'ClBr', 'Br'
missing_features: no sulfonamide, sulfone or other sulfonyl acceptor in any of the 870 proposals, although the seed pool supplied one
no nitrile anywhere, so no small strongly polar terminal acceptor is available
no saturated azacycle at all; piperidine, piperazine and morpholine rings match 0.000 of the set
no trifluoromethyl or other gem-polyhalogenated carbon, although 94.5 percent of molecules carry a halogen
biaryl linkage nearly vanishes, 0.6 percent of proposals against 40 percent of the supplied starting molecules
no defined stereochemistry at all; digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 over the whole set
per_task.score_gradient_reading: By score quintile the gradient rewards one thing above all: a halogen bonded directly to nitrogen rises from 16 percent of the bottom quintile to 56 percent of the top, and 60 percent of the thirty best, while basic amine content falls the other way, 16 percent to 3 percent, and hydrogen-bond donors drop 1.6 to 1.4. Size, ring count and aromatic ring count are flat across the top four quintiles, 24.7 to 25.2 heavy atoms and 3.0 rings, so the climb from 0.25 to 0.43 is bought entirely by peripheral heteroatom substitution on a fixed core, not by any scaffold change.

per_task.generated_character: The most bloated set of the five. Mean 854 Da and 62.2 heavy atoms over the whole proposal set, 8.16 rings of which 6.98 are aromatic, 62.4 percent above 600 Da, longest SMILES 236 characters, and only 10.3 percent satisfying all four Lipinski criteria. Two distinct regimes exist. One seed converged on a compact pyrimidinyl-pyridine biaryl fused to an oxazinone, mean 538 Da in the top thirty, decorated with nitriles and cyanate esters. The other two grew sprawling multi-ring assemblies of xanthine-like diazinediones stitched to pyridines, such as the endpoint molecule 'C=CN(C)C(=O)N(C=C)C(Nc1nc2c(C)cc1-2)n1c(=O)n(CF)c(=O)c2c3n(cc21)-c1nc(C(C)=O)cc(c1C)-c1cnccc1-3' at 0.5902. The score floor is 0.5000 and is reached by anything at all, including 'C#C' and the polyene 'C=CC=C(C=C)C(C=CC)=CC=C', so most of the set sits in a very flat band from 0.5000 to 0.6220.
liabilities: aryl cyanate and thiocyanate esters carry the entire top band: 'Cc1c(OC#N)ncc(-c2nccc(-c3nc(=O)oc4nc(OC(C)(C)F)c(C#N)c(C(C)C#N)c34)n2)c1F' and 'CC#COc1nc2oc(=O)nc(-c3ccnc(-c4cnc(OC)c(C#N)c4Br)n3)c2c(SC#N)c1C#N'
tertiary alkyl fluorides on an ether carbon, 'COc1ncc(-c2nccc(-c3nc(=O)oc4nc(OC(C)(C)F)c(C#N)c(C(C)C#N)c34)n2)c(Cl)c1C', which solvolyse on contact with water
peroxide O-O linkages in 32.2 percent of the whole proposal set
aminal and N-acyl aminal centres with a hydrazine N-N on top, 'C=CN(Nc1nc2c(C)cc1-2)C(=O)N(C=O)C(Nc1nc2c(C)cc1-2)n1c(=O)n(C)c(=O)c2c3n(cc21)-c1cc(C(=O)CC)cc(c1C)-c1cnccc1-3'
the bulk of the set is 850 to 1100 Da with 10 to 15 rotatable bonds, outside any oral-drug envelope
missing_features: no hydrogen-bond donor at all in the thirty best, so no amide or aniline NH is offered to the objective
no amide in the top band, 0 of the thirty best, although 17.6 percent of the whole set has one
no basic nitrogen in the top band and only 7.2 percent across the set
no sulfonyl, sulfonamide or sulfone acceptor in any of the 870 proposals
no saturated linker ring; piperidine, piperazine and morpholine match 0.2 percent and saturated carbocycles 0.0 percent
no reliable way to shrink; the winning compact cores arose in only one of the three seeds
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient rewards shrinking, not growing. The top score quintile averages 537 Da and 4.27 rings against 942 to 1094 Da and 9.2 to 12.2 rings in quintiles two to four, logP 3.48 against 7.34, and zero hydrogen-bond donors against 1.2. Overlaid on that, aryl cyanate or thiocyanate esters go from 3 percent of the lower quintiles to 89 percent of the top quintile and 90 percent of the thirty best, and the thirty best average 2.97 nitriles each against 0.03 in the Parent's own thirty best. The whole measured gradient is therefore a four-ring biaryl heteroaryl core, no donors, and as many small linear acceptors as can be hung on it.

per_task.generated_character: The widest score span of the five, 0.00017 to 0.9781, and the greasiest chemistry. The whole proposal set averages 702 Da, logP 8.31, 12.1 rotatable bonds and 98.2 percent halogenated (digest halogen_rate 0.9816), and only 7.2 percent satisfy all four Lipinski criteria. The winning series is a single diaryl ether scaffold - 80 of one seed's 290 proposals share the Murcko scaffold c1ccc(Oc2ccccc2)cc1 - carrying a long flexible chain that terminates in a secondary alkylamine: 'C=C(CCc1cc(F)cc(Oc2ccc(S)cc2S)c1N)CC(Cl)NCC' at 0.9781. The other two seeds never found it and ended on different, more bridged frameworks at 0.7315 and 0.8699, which is where the per-seed spread comes from. 96.0 percent of proposals carry at least one undefined stereocentre, averaging 2.19 of them, and none is ever specified.
liabilities: alpha-chloroamines in 46.7 percent of the thirty best, 'C=C(CCc1cc(F)cc(Oc2ccc(S)cc2S)c1N)CC(Cl)NCC', which are alkylating and not isolable

aryl hypohalites, an O-F and an O-Br directly on a phenol oxygen, in 46.7 percent of the thirty best: 'C=C(CCc1cc(F)cc(Oc2cccc(C)c2OF)c1C)CC(Cl)NCC' and 'C=C(CCc1cc(F)cc(Oc2cccc(C)c2OBr)c1)CCC(NC)NCC'
an S-Br sulfenyl bromide, 'C=C(CCc1cc(F)cc(Oc2cccc(C)c2SBr)c1)CCC(NC)NCCF'
free aromatic thiols including a benzene-1,2-dithiol in the single best molecule, oxidation-labile and a frequent assay artefact

cyclopropene rings in 13.1 percent of the set and strained bridged polycyclics at the endpoints, 'CNc1cc(Cl)c(Cl)c(OC2C=C2CCc2cc3c4c(c2)C(C3)C4(C)N)c1' and 'CC1(N)C2=CC3C=C(CCC4=C(Br)C4Oc4cc(N)cc(Cl)c4Cl)C=C2C1C3'
50.8 percent of proposals exceed 600 Da and mean logP is 8.31, so most of the oracle budget is spent well outside any plausible envelope
missing_features: the basic nitrogen is never placed in a ring; piperazine, piperidine and morpholine all match 0.000 of the 870 proposals, so the amine is always a chain amine
no rigid two- to three-carbon aryl-to-amine linker; the thirty best average 11.1 rotatable bonds, so the pharmacophore distance is never fixed
no defined stereochemistry at the 2.19 undefined centres per molecule the winners carry
no trifluoromethyl or other gem-polyhalogen group despite a 98.2 percent halogen rate
no way to trim lipophilicity; the thirty best still average logP 6.56 and nothing in the set pairs a basic amine with a polar ring heteroatom
no amide in any of the thirty best, so no directional donor-acceptor pair accompanies the amine
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The clearest gradient in the node and it points straight at a basic amine. A basic nitrogen is present in 84 percent of the top score quintile and in all thirty of the best molecules, against 26 to 40 percent of every lower quintile. The second axis is size: the top quintile averages 474 Da and 3.58 rings against 941 to 943 Da and 5.9 to 6.2 rings in the bottom two, and logP 6.56 against 9.3 to 10.3. The worst molecules are exactly the sulfonamide seed fragments that carry no basic centre at all, 'CC(=O)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1' and 'COS(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1' at 0.0002. The objective rewards a mid-sized aromatic bearing one accessible basic amine, and the generator reaches that only by growing a floppy aliphatic chain.

per_task.generated_character: The most conventional-looking chemistry of the five and the lowest ceiling, best 0.2305. Molecules average 435 Da, 31.8 heavy atoms, 5.51 rings of which only 2.10 are aromatic, fraction sp3 carbon 0.37, 1.87 amides each, and almost no halogen - digest halogen_rate 0.1609, the only task below 0.74. 88.5 percent satisfy all four Lipinski criteria. The recurring motif is a fused saturated diketopiperazine welded onto a dibenzoxazepine or a benzazepine, as in 'CCCN1C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C(C)C2=C3NN(CCC21)c1cc(OCC)ccc1Oc1ccccc13' at 0.2305. This is also the most diverse task: 181 to 201 distinct Murcko scaffolds per seed and 17 to 18 among the thirty best, against 2 to 7 elsewhere.
liabilities: hydrazine-type N-N single bonds inside the ring in 46.7 percent of the thirty best, 'CCCN1C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C(C)C2=C3NN(CCC21)c1cc(OCC)ccc1Oc1ccccc13', where the all-carbon analogue 'CCCN1C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C(C)C2=C3CN(CCC21)c1cc(OCC)ccc1Oc1ccccc13' scores 0.2276, so the liability buys almost nothing
bridged and spiro-fused systems in 70 percent of the thirty best, several with implausible fusions such as 'CCOc1c2cc-2c2c1CC(C)N1C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)NCC1c1ccc(cc1)CN2C'
an N-fluoro lactam in the endpoint molecule 'CCCc1c2cc(OCC)c(c1CC)CN1C2=C(C)N(C)CN(F)C(=O)CC1c1ccccc1'
aminal N-C-N centres in 8.2 percent of the set, hydrolytically labile next to the adjacent amide
1.6 percent of the budget spent on one- and two-atom fragments: 'C', 'C#C', 'CNN'
missing_features: no carboxylic acid, 0.6 percent, and no tetrazole or other acid isostere anywhere in the 870 proposals
no defined stereochemistry although 80.3 percent of proposals carry an undefined stereocentre, 1.46 per molecule, on cores that are three-quarters saturated
clean saturated azacycles are nearly absent, 2.9 percent, so the basic nitrogen the gradient rewards sits in fused or bridged fragments instead
no trifluoromethyl and almost no halogen at all, 16.1 percent, so the lipophilic handle the gradient rewards is reachable only by adding alkyl chains
no sulfonamide or sulfone, 0.2 percent, as an alternative polar anchor
per_task.score_gradient_reading: A weak, broad gradient with a narrow dynamic range, 0.1395 to 0.2126 between bottom and top quintile means. What moves with score is basic nitrogen, 32 percent to 58 percent, ring count 4.67 to 5.67, lipophilicity 2.36 to 4.32, and amide content - all thirty of the best carry at least one amide, 1.83 on average. Aromatic ring count does not move, 2.44 to 1.97, so the objective rewards a saturated, fused, amide-rich and weakly basic body rather than more aromatic surface. The worst molecules are bare fragments, 'C', 'C#C', 'CNN'.

per_task.generated_character: Compact and the most heavily fluorinated set: mean 367 Da, 26.1 heavy atoms, 3.76 rings of which 2.36 are aromatic, 87.2 percent halogenated with fluorine on essentially all of those, and 99.7 percent satisfying all four Lipinski criteria. Nearly the whole proposal set is one xanthine-like pyrrolo-pyrimidinedione core, carried by 61 to 114 of each seed's 290 proposals, with a small sp3 or cyclopentadiene ring hung off the pyrrole nitrogen and fluoroalkyl chains on the two imide nitrogens, as in 'N=c1c2c(CCF)n(C3C(O)=CC=C3CF)cc2n(F)c(=O)n1CCF' at 0.6278. One seed collapsed hardest, to 41 distinct Murcko scaffolds across 290 proposals and 2 among the thirty best. The score span is proportionally the widest, 3.7e-42 to 0.6527, because unsubstituted fragments such as 'F', 'FF' and 'FS' score at or near zero.
liabilities: N-fluoro imide and N-fluoro azole nitrogens in 80 percent of the thirty best: 'COC1=NC(F)C1(F)n1cc2c(c1-c1ccccc1)c(=N)n(C)c(=O)n2F' and 'N=c1c2c(CCF)n(C3C(O)=CC=C3CF)cc2n(F)c(=O)n1CCF' are fluorinating agents, not stable candidates
a terminal thioaldehyde on a polyene, 'COC1=NC(F)C1n1cc2c(c1C=C(F)C=CC=S)c(=N)n(C)c(=O)n2F', which cannot be isolated
a four-membered azete ring bearing two fluorines and a methoxy imidate in the best molecule; 56.7 percent of the thirty best contain a three- or four-membered ring
cyclopentadienol enols in 43.3 percent of the thirty best, 'Cc1c2c(=N)n(CCF)c(=O)n(F)c2cn1C1C(O)=CC=C1F', which tautomerise away immediately
a free thiol in 10 percent of the thirty best, 'N=c1c2c(CS)n(C3(F)C(O)=CC=C3CF)cc2n(F)c(=O)n1CCF'
3.6 percent of proposals, the highest of the five tasks, are one- and two-atom fragments: 'F', 'FF', 'FS'
missing_features: no trifluoromethyl in any of the 870 proposals although fluorine is on 87.2 percent of them; every fluorine is a lone substituent
no free primary amine on an sp3 carbon and no basic centre at all in the thirty best, 0 of 30
no defined stereochemistry although 65.7 percent of proposals carry an undefined stereocentre, 1.36 per molecule
no saturated azacycle, 0.3 percent, and no saturated carbocycle at all, so the sp3 ring is always an unsaturated cyclopentadiene or a strained azetine
no amide in the top band, 3.3 percent of the thirty best, and no carboxylic acid anywhere in the set
ether oxygens collapse to 28.0 percent of proposals, the lowest of the five tasks, so polar acceptors come only from the fixed core
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Monotone in two features and nothing else. A halogen bonded to nitrogen, almost always an N-fluoro on a ring nitrogen, rises from 22 percent of the bottom score quintile to 59 percent of the top and 80 percent of the thirty best; the thirty best also average 3.03 fluorines against 1.97 across the set. Molecular weight, logP and polar surface area are essentially constant across the top four quintiles, 375 to 382 Da, logP 2.1, TPSA 77, so the entire climb from 0.0019 to 0.4633 is fluorine and N-fluorine placement on a frozen core. Basic nitrogen is absent from all thirty of the best.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A halogen bonded directly to nitrogen appears in 56 percent and 59 percent of the top score quintile on two objectives and in 60 percent and 80 percent of their thirty best molecules; on a third, a halogen bonded directly to a phenol oxygen appears in 46.7 percent of the thirty best and an S-Br in 16.7 percent. Concrete cases are 'COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=NBr)N(Br)c3ccccc3)cc2c(OC)c1C', 'C=C(CCc1cc(F)cc(Oc2cccc(C)c2OF)c1C)CC(Cl)NCC' and 'C=C(CCc1cc(F)cc(Oc2cccc(C)c2SBr)c1)CCC(NC)NCCF'. These are the highest-scoring molecules the generator produced, not stragglers, so score is being climbed through bonds that cannot exist on a bench.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator attaches halogens to heteroatoms, producing N-X, O-X and S-X bonds that no chemist would call isolable.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The halogen substitution step in the mutation menu is applied per atom with no valence-context restriction. Restricting halogen attachment to carbon, and filtering N-X, O-X and S-X bonds at proposal time, would close the dominant decoration channel the current search relies on; a generator that keeps the channel should at least be measured on how much of its score sits on it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Piperidine, piperazine and morpholine rings match 0.0 to 2.9 percent of each objective's 870 proposals and a 1,4-diazinane matches at most 0.2 percent, against 1 of the 10 supplied starting molecules. An unfused saturated six-carbon ring matches exactly none of the 4350 proposals read. Where a basic nitrogen does appear it is a chain amine, as in 'C=C(CCc1cc(F)cc(Oc2ccc(S)cc2S)c1N)CC(Cl)NCC' and 'C=C(CCc1cc(F)cc(Oc2cccc(C)c2OBr)c1)CCC(NC)NCC', which push the thirty best on that objective to 11.1 rotatable bonds. Yet a basic nitrogen is present in 84 percent and 58 percent of the top score quintile on two objectives, so the feature its own best molecules need is one it can only improvise.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot build a saturated nitrogen heterocycle, so every basic amine it makes is an acyclic chain amine.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction is limited to closures the crossover and atom/bond mutations happen to make, and the fragment vocabulary carries no intact saturated azacycle. Ring-level insertion and ring-replacement operators drawn from a small set of common saturated heterocycles would let the search place a basic centre at a fixed geometry instead of growing a chain to reach it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on all five objectives and not one of the 4350 proposals read has an '@' in its SMILES. The molecules are not achiral: 96.0 percent of one objective's set has at least one undefined tetrahedral centre, averaging 2.19 per molecule, and 80.3 percent and 65.7 percent on two others, including the endpoint molecules 'CNc1cc(Cl)c(Cl)c(OC2C=C2CCc2cc3c4c(c2)C(C3)C4(C)N)c1' and 'CCCN1C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C(C)C2=C3NN(CCC21)c1cc(OCC)ccc1Oc1ccccc13'.
transferable_gaps.gap: No proposal ever carries defined stereochemistry, although most of them have stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Configuration is not a search variable: the graph operators never set it and the canonical-identity and duplicate-rejection step collapses stereoisomers into one molecule, so a scoring function sensitive to 3D arrangement cannot be optimized and a chosen molecule is under-specified. Carrying and mutating stereo-tags, and treating distinct configurations as distinct identities, is the change.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest charged_rate is 0.0 on all five objectives. Carboxylic acids are present in 2 of the 10 supplied starting molecules, including 'COc1cc(F)cc(-c2ccc(C(CC(=O)O)NC(=O)C3CCCN3S(=O)(=O)c3cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c3)cc2)c1' and 'CCCN(CCc1cccc(-c2ccccc2)c1)C(=O)C1OC(C(=O)O)=CC(N)C1NC(C)=O', but fall to 0.0 to 12.8 percent of proposals and to 0 of the thirty best on every objective. Tetrazoles, sulfonates, phosphonates and quaternary nitrogens match none of the 4350 proposals; the element census never includes phosphorus or boron.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no ionisable group and no formal charge, losing the acidic handles its own starting pool contained.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Acid and salt-bridge chemistry is outside the reachable space of the current operators, so any reward that depends on an ionised contact is unreachable regardless of search effort. A fragment vocabulary containing acidic heads and their common isosteres, with operators that can graft one, is the missing capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Fluorine is extremely common - digest halogen_rate 0.9816, 0.9448 and 0.8724 on three objectives, and 4412 fluorine atoms across the proposal set - yet a C(F)(F)F group matches exactly none of the 4350 proposals read, and the same holds for the Parent's trajectories read under the same procedure. The fluorines land as single ring substituents or on heteroatoms, as in 'N=c1c2c(CCF)n(C3C(O)=CC=C3CF)cc2n(F)c(=O)n1CCF'.
transferable_gaps.gap: Multi-halogen carbon groups are unreachable; halogens are placed one atom at a time and a trifluoromethyl is never assembled.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Halogen placement is a single-atom substitution with no gem-polysubstitution step and no pre-built halogenated fragment in the vocabulary, so one of the most common lipophilicity and metabolic-stability handles in real medicinal chemistry is structurally out of reach. Supplying polyhalogenated carbon fragments as insertion units is the change.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Mean molecular weight reaches 854 Da on one objective and 702 Da on another, with 62.4 percent and 50.8 percent of proposals above 600 Da and longest SMILES of 236 and 237 characters. On both, the score gradient points the other way: the top score quintile averages 537 Da and 474 Da against 941 to 1094 Da in the lower quintiles, and logP 3.48 and 6.56 against 7.3 to 10.3. The compact winning core was found by only one of the three seeds on one of them, while the other two ended on sprawling fused assemblies such as 'C=CN(Nc1nc2c(C)cc1-2)C(=O)N(C=O)C(Nc1nc2c(C)cc1-2)n1c(=O)n(C)c(=O)c2c3n(cc21)-c1cc(C(=O)CC)cc(c1C)-c1cnccc1-3'.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecule size only grows; the generator has no reliable way to shrink a candidate back down.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Crossover fuses whole fragments and mutation adds atoms, so mass accumulates monotonically within a lineage and the only path back to a smaller molecule is a lucky deletion. A fragment-excision operator, or a size-aware proposal distribution that samples shrinking edits as often as growing ones, would let the search follow a gradient that rewards compactness instead of needing the right seed to stumble on it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Between 1.6 and 3.6 percent of each objective's proposals have six or fewer heavy atoms and sit at the score floor: 'Br', 'OO', 'ClBr', 'C1COO1', 'C', 'C=C', 'C#C', 'CNN', 'F', 'FF', 'FS'. One is the very last proposal of a seed, 'C1COO1' at evaluation 300 scoring 0.0, so the collapse is not confined to early exploration. At roughly 2.8 percent of a 290-proposal budget this is eight to ten wasted evaluations per run.
transferable_gaps.gap: Delete-type edits are unguarded and collapse molecules into one- and two-atom fragments that burn oracle calls.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation operators can strip a molecule down to a single atom and the proposal path accepts the result as a valid distinct candidate. A minimum-heavy-atom guard with a retry on degenerate edits would return that budget to the search without touching any selection or model behaviour.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the proposal set the ring-size census is 136 three-membered and 1458 four-membered rings against 4318 five- and 13644 six-membered, and an unfused saturated six-carbon ring matches none of the 4350 proposals. Strained rings reach the winners: 56.7 percent of one objective's thirty best contain a three- or four-membered ring, including the azete in 'COC1=NC(F)C1(F)n1cc2c(c1-c1ccccc1)c(=N)n(C)c(=O)n2F'; cyclopropenes appear in 13.1 percent of another set, as in 'CNc1cc(Cl)c(Cl)c(OC2C=C2CCc2cc3c4c(c2)C(C3)C4(C)N)c1'; and a strained benzo-fused four-ring carries the single best molecule on a third, 'Cc1cc2c(c(C)c1C)C=C2CC(=O)N(O)c1ccc(Br)nc1'.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring formation favours strained three- and four-membered closures and never produces a plain saturated carbocycle.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring closures bond whatever two atoms the operator picks, with no ring-size or strain preference and no saturated-ring fragments in the vocabulary. Weighting closures toward five- and six-membered rings, and supplying intact common saturated rings as insertion units, would move the generated sp3 content from strained curiosities to chemistry a chemist could order.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Accepted-only task-local chronological archive, bounded greedy 64-member survivor population and score-quantile parent sampling.

Connected-fragment crossover, optional post-crossover mutation and ordinary one-, two- and three-call mutation continuation with bounded retries and saturation rules; all seven atom, bond and ring mutation families at unchanged weights.

Disabled direct aromatic C/N exchange with passive withheld-menu tracing; stable canonical isomeric identity with original-graph reuse; initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection; fixed 160-member pools and announced batches of ten.
Sulfur introduction gate: per-signature maximum over the actual scored generating parents with the fixed neutral envelope at final novel pool admission, with bounded refill and passive receipts.

Count-Morgan features with shared cache, generalized Tanimoto Gaussian process, accepted-data normalization with 0.001 floor, 0.05 observation noise, full latent covariance and full jittered Cholesky.

Nonzero Gaussian marginal residual influence at the jittered marginal variances from the original single normal-array draw, stable masked first-index selection, identity-bound predictions and next-fit probes; cross-candidate residual correlation is removed.
Finite guards, jitter schedule and first-valid-pool numerical fallback, source-preserved but not exercised beyond the first jitter.
